subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw trust and adopt these exact 14 upstream action revisions in workflows that handle credentials, publishing, scanners, and Codex agents?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but accepting new third-party executable revisions across privileged workflows is a repository trust decision that automated review cannot make for maintainers.

options.title: Approve the grouped revisions
options.body: Verify the upstream tags and final exact-head checks, then merge all consistent full-SHA updates together.

options.title: Split sensitive action families
options.body: Separate Codex, token, Docker-publishing, and scanner revisions from lower-privilege setup and repository-maintenance updates for narrower review.

options.title: Pause the update
options.body: Keep the existing pins until a workflow owner can provide dedicated revision and release-path verification.

recommendation.title: Approve the grouped revisions
recommendation.body: Verify the upstream tags and final exact-head checks, then merge all consistent full-SHA updates together.

likelyOwner.reason: The history and timeline most strongly connect steipete to release workflow ownership and this PR's maintainer routing.
